findings.title: ToStringMapIntE/ToStringMapInt64E panic on maps with non-string keys
findings.property: for any map input the function returns a result or an error, never panics; key count is preserved on success
findings.expected: map[string]int{"0": 0} (keys converted like the map[any]T case uses ToString) or at least a non-nil error
findings.actual: panic: reflect.Value.SetMapIndex: value of type int is not assignable to type string (map.go:191)
findings.evidence: The function is an E-variant that returns an error for uncastable input; the reflect fallback is explicitly meant to accept arbitrary map kinds, and sibling ToStringMapStringE returns an error (not a panic) for map[int]string. The map[any]T and map[any]any branches convert keys with ToString, but the reflect fallback passes the original key to SetMapIndex.

error.message: reflect.Value.SetMapIndex: value of type int is not assignable to type string

review.title: ToStringMapIntE/ToStringMapInt64E panic on maps with non-string keys (reflect fallback)
review.reason: In toStringMapIntE (map.go:178-192), any map kind that misses the typed cases reaches the reflect fallback. That fallback calls SetMapIndex on a map[string]T with the original key, so any non-string key type, such as map[int]int, panics with 'value of type int is not assignable to type string'. The fallback's existing error check shows it is meant to return an error for uncastable input, and the map[any]T and map[any]any cases already convert keys with ToString. An E-variant taking `any` should return a result or an error, not panic, so a maintainer would take a small fix: convert the key with ToStringE, or return an error.

fix.reason: the repro passes on the patched code

findings.title: ToStringMapStringSliceE treats map[any]string values differently from map[string]string
findings.property: map[any]string{k: v} and map[string]string{k: v} convert to the same map[string][]string
findings.expected: map["k":["a b"]], same as the map[string]string case, which wraps each string value in a one-element slice
findings.actual: map["k":["a" "b"]]; and for value "" the result is an empty slice instead of [""]
findings.evidence: The map[string]string branch does m[k] = []string{val}; the map[any]string branch calls ToStringSlice(val), which whitespace-splits the string, so equivalent inputs give different outputs and strings with spaces are split / empty strings dropped.

error.message: map[any]string gave map["k":["a" "b"]], map[string]string gave map["k":["a b"]]

review.title: ToStringMapStringSliceE splits map[any]string values on whitespace but wraps map[string]string values
review.reason: The existing test in map_test.go (TestStringMapStringSlice) explicitly expects map[any]string{"key 1":"value 1"} to give {"value","1"} (stringMapStringSingleSliceFieldsResult). The same test expects the map[any]any case to split too, and expects map[string]string to give a single-element slice. The map[any]* branches deliberately route through ToStringSlice, which uses strings.Fields. The inconsistency is real but it is tested, intentional, long-standing behavior, and changing it would break existing callers and tests.
